analysis: Examined the ProviderLoop.swift head (lines 1-1191) and the DaemonState+Coding.swift patch. The changes in ProviderLoop.swift add new actor state at head lines 705-716: selectedModelRecovery, a test-only selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (nil in production), savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. Head line 868 seeds savedEnabledModels from config.backend.enabledModels. DaemonState+Coding adds optional, decodeIfPresent fields to the daemon state file: enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. These are operator-facing diagnostics, namely model IDs already present in local configuration. The daemon state file is local, operator-owned status (TB-003). None of these fields are keys, tokens, prompts or attestation material, so the change creates no new information-disclosure surface. Adding optional keys is backward compatible for decoding. No changes touch the following: keyPair generation (line 908, A-003), the signer or attestationBuilder (A-002, A-010), advertisedModels filtering, modelHashes/liveModelHashes (T-012, T-027), the SendHandle ordering barrier (T-008) or prefix-cache storage (T-041). The recovery logic lives in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, which was not supplied. Integration should confirm that the recovery load: respects advertisedModels, retiringModels and failedSelfTestHashes (the ABA self-test guard at lines 422-430); does not bypass the drain, update or shutdown admission gates; and runs the weight-hash refresh so that attestation reports the hashes actually being served. The test override seam should also be confirmed unreachable in production. No regression was identified in the supplied units.
